points.text: Tool activity alone does not establish customer value.
Turn recurring mistakes into checks and shared blueprints.
Track flow, failures, rework and customer outcomes.
Keep intent available to implementation, QA and operations.
Separate implementation from QA; combine adaptive and deterministic checks.
Feed production findings into the next plan and review.
Build tools for your own work and validate the outputs.
Give permissions, logs and recovery explicit attention.
Maintain shared AI assets as software products.
Give people a probe they can inspect and challenge.
Test the understanding of the problem as well as the solution.
As building accelerates, ideas, orchestration and validation matter more.
Help people envision outcomes and express what they need.
Evaluate both generation and the experience of using the result.
Questions can help, but repetitive or irrelevant prompts obstruct exploration.
Work with legal specialists on regulatory and contract restrictions.
Back leadership expectations with guidance, training and community.
Give tools and quotas clear ownership and visibility.
Put agents where the work and its context already happen.
Separate contribution, merge, CI and production permissions.

cards.headline: A prototype still needs a production path

points.text: Include architecture, access, release, operations and support.
Make control ownership and approval boundaries explicit.
Start with a bounded value stream and measure accepted delivery.
The cost of repetition shapes which questions are feasible.
Preserve configurations and invest in orchestration.
When results are unstable, examine the premise and methodology.
Check whether a change preserves the wider system.
Record decision reasons, constraints and rejected options.
Combine deterministic checks with human judgement and value gates.
